encounters.cc: Progressive pain in both hands worsening over the past year, worse in the morning but improving with activity.

lines: Progressive pain in both hands worsening over the past year, worse in the morning but improving with activity.
The patient with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and prior open-angle glaucoma evaluation presents with hand pain that has been progressively worsening over the past year.
She reports that the pain is worse in the morning but improves with activity throughout the day.
She denies any redness or warmth over the joints.
Her medical history is significant for hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Latanoprost 0.005% ophthalmic solution 1 drop OU at bedtime
- Gabapentin 300 mg PO three times daily
- Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hyperlipidemia; died of myocardial infarction age 72
Smoking: Current smoker, 1 pack per day for 35 years (35 pack-years).
On physical examination, you note bony enlargements of the distal and proximal interphalangeal joints of both hands.
There is mild tenderness on palpation of these joints, and crepitus is felt with passive movement.
No erythema or warmth is noted.
An X-ray of the hands is performed and shows decreased joint space, subchondral sclerosis, and periarticular osteophytes in the affected joints.

lines: Gradually worsening right knee pain over the past 6 months with morning stiffness lasting less than 20 minutes.

She finds it difficult to get up after prolonged sitting and complains that her knees feel stiff in the morning but improve within 20 minutes.

- Gabapentin 300 mg PO three times daily
- Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hyperlipidemia; died of myocardial infarction age 72

The patient is interested in reducing the long-term burden of her symptoms.

lines: Persistent burning pain on the right side of the chest for 5 months following an episode of shingles.
The patient is a 67-year-old female with primary open-angle glaucoma and osteoarthritis who returns for evaluation of persistent pain.
She reports that the pain began after an episode of shingles, which was treated with valacyclovir.
The pain is described as sharp and shooting, worsening with light touch.
She has tried over-the-counter acetaminophen and ibuprofen with no significant relief.
Her medical history is significant for hypertension, controlled with hydrochlorothiazide, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, managed with metformin.
- Latanoprost 0.005% ophthalmic solution 1 drop OU at bedtime
- Gabapentin 300 mg PO three times daily
- Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hyperlipidemia; died of myocardial infarction age 72

encounters.cc: Worsening bilateral knee pain and new bony enlargements in the finger joints.

lines: Worsening bilateral knee pain and new bony enlargements in the finger joints.
She returns with progression of osteoarthritis following rheumatology evaluation in 2020 and orthopedic evaluations in 2021 and 2022.
She describes the pain as aching and stiff, especially after prolonged standing or walking.
The discomfort improves with rest but worsens throughout the day.
She has also noticed bony enlargements around the joints of her fingers.
Her medical history is notable for obesity and hypertension.
- Latanoprost 0.005% ophthalmic solution 1 drop OU at bedtime
- Gabapentin 300 mg PO three times daily
- Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hyperlipidemia; died of myocardial infarction age 72

Her symptoms are worse on the right than the left.
Synovial fluid analysis shows low white blood cell count.
A study is conducted to analyze the chondrocyte secretions in affected joints.

encounters.cc: Progressively worsening forgetfulness, disorientation, and word-finding difficulties over the past 18 months.

lines: Progressively worsening forgetfulness, disorientation, and word-finding difficulties over the past 18 months.

This 69-year-old female with hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hyperlipidemia, and history of primary open-angle glaucoma, osteoarthritis, and postherpetic neuralgia presents to the Psychiatry clinic.
She is brought to the clinic by her daughter due to progressively worsening forgetfulness and disorientation over the past 18 months.
The patient has misplaced common household items, gotten lost driving on familiar roads, and occasionally struggles to find the correct words when speaking.
She also displays increased irritability and minor personality changes, which are new for her.
Her medical history is significant for well-controlled hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Latanoprost 0.005% ophthalmic solution 1 drop OU at bedtime
- Gabapentin 300 mg PO three times daily
- Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hyperlipidemia; died of myocardial infarction age 72
Smoking: Current smoker, 1 pack per day for 35 years (35 pack-years).
She is oriented to person but not to place or time.
Neurologic examination shows no focal deficits.
Her Mini-Mental State Examination score is 22/30.
MRI of the brain reveals diffuse cortical atrophy, most pronounced in the hippocampus and temporal lobes.
